issues.problem: The claim that official render.py renders fp32 positions / unquantised opacity from the saved PLY is wrong for commit 710ebab8. render.py -> Scene(load_iteration=-1) -> Scene.__init__ takes the 'if self.loaded_iter: print("Load bitstream!"); self.gaussians.decode(model_path/bitstream)' branch, never load_ply. GaussianModel.decode reads position.npz (fp16 -> fp32), dequantises 8-bit opacity (q*step+min in logit domain), and takes codebook rows for scale/rot/dc/SH. The paper CSV numbers (metrics.py after render.py) are therefore computed on the DECODED bitstream. The PLY written by scene.save at 30000 is not read by render.py. Only the in-training 'Evaluating test' print at iteration 30000 (before the apply/encode block) is fp32/unquantised, and it also renders with STE masks.
issues.evidence: source/code/scene/__init__.py: 'if self.loaded_iter: print("Load bitstream!"); self.gaussians.decode(os.path.join(self.model_path, "bitstream"))'; render.py render_sets uses Scene(dataset, gaussians, load_iteration=iteration); train.py calls training_report before the 'Apply mask' block.

evaluation_mode_judgement.reason: Official render.py decodes the bitstream, so the fp16 positions and 8-bit opacity are part of the paper numbers.
evaluation_mode_judgement.estimated_difference_decoded_vs_fp32: Positions: fp16 half-ulp is about 4.9e-4 x |x|, i.e. about 2e-3 to 5e-3 at |x| of 5 to 10 (typical Mip-NeRF 360 COLMAP extents), sub-pixel for most views. Opacity: 8 bits over the logit range gives a step of about 0.08 logit, so under 1% relative error. Expected 0.01-0.05 dB, possibly slightly above 0.05 dB on outdoor scenes with far-from-origin foreground (bicycle, stump, treehill). This is an estimate, not measured: the smoke run has no fp32 comparison. It is moot for matching the paper because the official numbers include it.

paper_results_check: Per-scene PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/size/Gaussian counts match App. Tab. A.6/A.7 and results/MipNeRF360/*.csv (size_bytes/1e6; baseline row equals the highest-rate row). Averages 27.05 / 0.802 / 0.239 / 23.46 and the rate-point averages equal Tab. A.3. T&T and DB per-scene and average values equal Tab. A.1/A.2/A.5 (means re-computed and consistent). 3DGS baseline rows match. Only the 'notes' string about official evaluation is wrong (see the major issue).
summary: No critical issues. Gaussian mask, three SH masks (STE, lr 0.01/0.05, thresholds 0.1, L_SH over GS-kept rows), the six ECVQ codebooks and attribute split (3/4/3/9/15/21), unsquared L2 assignment, softmax entropy models, k-means init at 15001, reactivation 16000-20000 at p<=1e-5, rate-constrained assignment from 20001, the 10-step index refresh with a global cache, the x0.1 milestone after 12000 VQ steps, the /N/55 weights and the encode/decode path all match the official code operator by operator. Size = sum of the five official files / 1e6. The one major issue is the incorrect claim that the official evaluation is fp32/unquantised: render.py decodes the bitstream, so decoded is the correct primary mode, and the 'official' option and docs should be corrected.
